title: revertCommit cannot restore an `object` overlay at all — it passes no write intent, so restoreVersion defaults to `override-artifact` and the repository answers NOT_OVERRIDABLE
body:
Found while implementing #6215 (the package-scoping half of the same call). Recording only, per Prime Directive #10 — it is a different cause on a different line, outside that issue's ruled file surface.

## Evidence

`ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.revertCommit` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, the `existedBefore` limb) restores an edited artifact with:

```ts
await repo.restoreVersion(ref, it.prevVersion, {
    actor,
    source: 'protocol.revertCommit',
    message: `revert commit ${request.commitId}`,
});
```

No `intent`. `SysMetadataRepository.restoreVersion` therefore defaults to `intent: opts.intent ?? 'override-artifact'`, and `put` opens with `assertAllowed(ref.type, opts.intent)`, which refuses any type whose registry entry is not `allowOrgOverride`. `object` is exactly such a type, so every `object` item in a reverted commit comes back in `failed[]`:

```
[NOT_OVERRIDABLE] 'object' is not allowOrgOverride in the registry.
Overlay-allowed: view, page, dashboard, app, action, report, dataset,
translation, email_template, book, permission, position, tool, skill.
Set OS_METADATA_WRITABLE to enable additional types at runtime.
```

Measured on a real `SysMetadataRepository` over an in-memory `sys_metadata` / `sys_metadata_history` double while writing #6215's pin tests: an `object` saved twice through `saveMetaItem` and then reverted through `revertCommit` returns `revertedCount: 0`, `failedCount: 1` with that message. Package binding is irrelevant — a package-less object fails identically.

## Why the sibling caller works

`rollbackMetaItem` derives the intent instead of defaulting it:

```ts
const artifactBacked = this.isArtifactBacked(singularType, request.name);
const intent: 'override-artifact' | 'runtime-only' = artifactBacked
    ? 'override-artifact' : 'runtime-only';
```

A runtime-created object (`_provenance: 'org'`, the shape Studio's package workspace produces) is not artifact-backed, so the per-item rollback passes `runtime-only` and the same repository line admits it. `revertCommit` never computes that, so the two user-facing revert paths disagree about what is revertable — for the metadata type Studio creates most.

## Why it matters

`revertCommit` is the package-commit "undo" (ADR-0067). A commit that edited an object — the common case for an AI-built or Studio-built app — reports partial failure and leaves the edit in place, while the same edit reverts fine one artifact at a time through the version-history revert. The failure is per item, so the revert also reports `success` overall with a populated `failed[]`, which reads as a flaky revert rather than a systematic refusal.

`rollbackToPackageCommit` reverts through the same loop, so it inherits this.

## Suggested direction (not a ruling)

Compute the intent from the artifact the same way `rollbackMetaItem` does, rather than defaulting it at the repository — the repository's default is right for callers that genuinely mean "override an artifact", and the bug is that this caller never states which of the two it is. Note `revertCommit` reverts a batch, so the intent is per item, not per call.

Related: #6215 (the package-scoping defect on the same `restoreVersion` call; its pin tests use `view` precisely because `object` cannot reach the scoping line), ADR-0067, ADR-0048.
